<reason>B carried the decisive word “usually” by widening the denominator beyond Orbán, Erdoğan, and Chávez to populists that govern, moderate, lose, and leave, including Syriza and northern European parties. B also exposed A’s credit/blame asymmetry and distinguished loss of faith in party elites from decay of elections and courts. A’s claim that anti-pluralist rhetoric is itself backsliding even under compliance never fully answered that conduct-based test.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2 was decisive: moderation cannot be dismissed as mere external restraint while radicalization is blamed on populism itself, making A’s theory unfalsifiable and weakening its account of constrained populist cases.</best_rebuttal>
